previous_article.dek: One single-point move, one card out of the lineup, and two prices that didn't budge. Here's where the NFL EDGE card stands today.

items.headline: The Vikings moneyline changed hands — and books
paragraphs: The MIN moneyline went from -125 on DraftKings to -126 on FanDuel since the last check — the only live card on today's card that actually moved. The model's fair price ticked along with it, from about -128 to about -129. It's still a BET and still in the latest publication, so the pick is live; the move is one point, which is noise, not a reason to chase.

items.headline: The Broncos spread is off the board
paragraphs: Denver's 2.5-point spread at -102 no longer appears in the latest card — it was dropped from the lineup, not carried over. It is not a current recommendation, so treat it as closed rather than as a live play.

items.headline: Chicago and the Jets held their lines
paragraphs: Two cards didn't budge. Chicago's moneyline sits at -166 with a model fair price around -171, and the Jets are plus money at +102 against a fair price near even. Both are still present in the latest card, so the prices in front of you are the live ones.

items.headline: Small moves are the news — don't overread them
paragraphs: Week 1 cards are still settling, and everything that changed today is the ordinary kind: a one-point tick on the Vikings, a book swap underneath it, and a Denver spread that got cut from the card. None of it rewrites a bet; it just tells you where the card stands right now.

The Denver removal is the only thing that changes your plan. A selection that's no longer in the latest publication shouldn't be treated as a live recommendation — if it was on your slip, that's the signal to drop it. The steady lines on Chicago and the Jets mean the prices you saw this morning are the prices still in front of you.

items.headline: MIN moneyline: -125 to -126, and the offer flipped to FanDuel
paragraphs: Against the last observation, the Vikings moneyline moved one point from -125 on DraftKings to -126, and the offer now shows up on FanDuel. The model's fair price sits around -129 (it was about -128). Still a live BET. A one-point tick plus a book switch is worth watching, not worth chasing.

items.headline: NYJ moneyline: +102 steady, fair price near even
paragraphs: The Jets are unchanged from the previous observation to the latest: +102. The model's fair price is around -100, so the plus-money quote is on a side the model sees close to a coin flip. Still live. For newer bettors, whether that quote drifts toward the fair price is the thing to keep an eye on.

items.headline: CHI moneyline: -166, unchanged
paragraphs: Chicago didn't move between the previous and latest observations: -166 with a model fair price near -171, still a live BET. When a line holds at your price, the decision is easy — the number you were quoted is still the real one.

items.headline: DEN spread 2.5 at -102: dropped, not current
paragraphs: The Broncos spread was previously offered at 2.5 points, -102. It is not present in the latest card. That's a removal, not a recommendation — leave it off the slip and don't treat it as a live play.

items.headline: The price in front of you is the only one that counts
paragraphs: For new bettors, the market-watch habit is simple: a card holding still (Chicago, the Jets) means the quote you're looking at is real, and a card that switched books (the Vikings) is worth reading twice so you don't place at the wrong price. A one-point move is noise — what matters is that you're betting the number you think you're betting, on the book you think you're on.
And when a pick disappears from the latest card, like Denver's spread did, treat it as closed. There's no edge in betting a line the card has already dropped.
